steps.instruction: Identify the resistor by its color bands and cylindrical shape.
Identify the LED by its clear/colored dome and two legs (anode and cathode).
Identify the battery by its cylindrical shape with positive and negative terminals.
Identify the switch by its toggle/lever mechanism.
Identify the breadboard by its grid of holes for connecting components.
Identify the jumper wire by its flexible insulation and metal connectors.
Identify the multimeter by its display, dial, and probe ports.

rules.feedback: Resistor identified. It limits current flow in a circuit.
LED identified. It emits light when current flows in the forward direction.
Battery identified. It provides the voltage source for the circuit.
Switch identified. It opens or closes the circuit path.
Breadboard identified. It allows temporary connections without soldering.
Jumper wire identified. It connects components on the breadboard.
Multimeter identified. It measures voltage, current, and resistance.

outcomes.title: All components identified
outcomes.description: You have successfully identified all basic electronic components needed for circuit building.

safeFailure.guidance: Look at the shape, markings, and terminals to identify each component.

narration.text: This is a resistor. Notice the colored bands that indicate its resistance value.
This is an LED — Light Emitting Diode. The longer leg is the anode (positive), the shorter is the cathode (negative).
This is a battery. The positive terminal is marked with a plus sign, the negative with a minus.
This is a switch. It controls whether current can flow through the circuit.
This is a breadboard. The holes are connected in rows and columns, allowing you to build circuits without soldering.
These are jumper wires. They connect components together on the breadboard.
This is a multimeter. It can measure voltage, current, and resistance to help you understand your circuit.

captions.text: Resistor — colored bands show resistance value.
LED — longer leg is anode (+), shorter is cathode (-).
Switch — opens or closes the circuit.
Breadboard — grid of connected holes for temporary circuits.
Jumper wire — connects components on the breadboard.
Multimeter — measures voltage, current, and resistance.
